Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 How does this game differ from Forest Shuffle? 3 Game Flow 4 Trees and Rivers 5 Animals and Plants 6 Effects and Bonuses 7 Checking the Clearing 8 Special Case 9 End of the Game Overview In Forest Shuffle: Smoky Mountains , you create a forest according to your own vision—will you focus on densely planted tree lines or varied river landscapes? Skillfully place animals and plants on trees and along rivers to earn the most points. Whether a mighty predator, a humble gatherer, or a water dweller, every creature has its own unique preferences. How does this game differ from Forest Shuffle? Forest Shuffle: Smoky Mountains is a standalone game in the Forest Shuffle universe. The following features are different from the base game: • River cards introduce a new card type to the game. • River cards are played horizontally as individual rivers or attached below a tree . • Some species can only live in water and must therefore be attached to river cards. They may not be attached to trees. Game Flow Choose one of two actions: A) Draw 2 cards : Either from the clearing or the deck ; you may combine these as you wish. You may never have more than 10 cards in your hand. B) Play 1 card : Pay the cost by placing the corresponding number of cards from your hand into the clearing, and play a card from your hand into your forest. If applicable, carry out its effect or bonus . Trees and Rivers Trees always show exactly one species. When you play a tree, you can either place it separately in your forest or place another card from your hand face down as a universal river under this tree . Whenever you play a tree (with or without a universal river), you then reveal the top card of the deck and place it in the clearing. Trees, rivers, and trees with rivers have a different number of slots where split cards can be attached: • Trees without a river have four slots: one each at the top, bottom, left, and right. • Rivers also have four slots: two at the top and two at the bottom. • Trees with a river have five slots: one each at the top, left, and right, and two at the bottom. Animals and Plants The split cards show different animals and plants. When playing a split card, you must place it in an empty slot on the corresponding side of a tree or river in your forest. Some split cards show the water requirement below their cost. • Trees without a river only accept cards without water requirement. • Stand-alone rivers only accept cards with water requirement. • Trees with a river accept any cards (with or without water requirement) at the top and to the left and right. Below the river, however, you may place only cards with water requirement. Effects and Bonuses These are resolved after playing a card. First the effect, then the bonus. • Effects are activated whenever you pay for and play a card. Immediate effects are activated immediately after playing, and permanent effects are activated whenever their condition is met. • Bonuses are only activated if you pay for the card with matching cards . To do this, all cards you use to pay must show the same tree symbol as the card just played.

---

A new continent awaits in the Forest Shuffle universe: After exploring Central Europe in Forest Shuffle and the wilds of southern England in Forest Shuffle – Dartmoor, this new standalone game invites players on a journey to North America.

As the third standalone game in the Forest Shuffle series, Forest Shuffle - Smoky Mountains takes us to this popular North American National Park. Building on the familiar gameplay of the series, it introduces new species and clever twists in mechanics. This keeping the experience as fresh as the bubbling waters on the new terrain cards!

Here’s what Forest Shuffle – Smoky Mountains is all about:

     New terrain types centered around water, playable on their own or tucked as universal waters under trees.
     New synergies between flora and fauna, all revolving around the element of water
     In addition to a variety of species around the water, the game is also home to various large animals, such as black bears or bobcats.


Once again, the player who collected the most points, wins.

Forest Shuffle - Smoky Mountains is manufactured from FSC-certified material.

—description from the publisher
community_text:
[Rating: 3/10] Hope/continue to draw to get the 30 point animals and few other combos really matter.  Deer/wolf/butterfly was a surprising oversight in the original game but this seems as bad.   FS+Alpine or Dartmoor +\-Exmoor are fantastic and I really enjoy both.

[Rating: 3/10] Much inferior to the original... I only with this was conceived as an expansion with rivers and fish... THAT would have made it an interesting variation... otherwise it is very much on rails and the 30pts cards will effectively swing the game, who draws them will just aim to play those and carry the game. Won't be playing it again.

[Rating: 4/10] Agree with some others here in bgg. There seems to be a predominant strategy with the 10/30s cards. Feels like you're just setting up for the 30 pts animals each game maybe combining woth one more. I also prefer better to play dartmoor (with or without the expansion) and FS (with expansions)

[Rating: 5/10] Feels like you're just setting up for the 30 pts animals each game. Enjoyed dartmoor and FS+ alpine better

[Rating: 5/10] This forest shuffle is the worst of the 3. I'v played 50 ish games on bga. If you don't play the fish + river strategy you basicly have 75% chance of losing. Dartmoor+ exmoor is way better. Moreover, 30 point cards are way too polarizing. Typical game is : 2 players go for fish +river strategy and whoever gets the most 30 point cards wins the game. Too bad cause it has intresting ideas and card powers but for god sake PLAYTEST YOUR GODDAMN GAMES IT'S YOUR JOB, IT'S NOT HARD. I figured out fish and some cards are overpowered from the 5th games i'v played, just put some tiny bit effort into your

[Rating: 6/10] It's Forest Shuffle with different animals.  Rivers add little/nothing.  But that's fine.  If you like the original, you'll like this.

[Rating: 6/10] I guess playing it on BGA would be a better experience. Due to lack of solo and tedious scoring. The cards that give passive ability like "When you play a tree, draw a card" are prone to be forgotten and then three turns later someone would ask if they can draw back the missed trigger. That won't be an issue on digital. There are so many less fiddly and accessible tableau builders like Wingspan Pocket, Castle Combo, Faraway  or even Creature Caravan...
